The blades clatter onto the counter. Miss Grau leans against the shelf and laughs softly. "Mother has seen you long since."

Durch das Tor der Seilerkapelle: Through the gate of the ropemakers' chapel

“Mag Ashdown. Marlowe has put a pretty price on my head, I hear. Come and get it.”

“Evidence room. If you want to borrow something: I need your signature. And your nerves.”

A green glow in a preserving jar. It knocks softly against the lid.

A tall mirror in a gilded frame. Your reflection looks tired. When you turn away, it turns a heartbeat too late.

Nothing can be seen with the naked eye. Perhaps you'd see more if you looked differently.

Eine Frau mit Lupe am Kettchen sitzt vor:
A woman with a loupe on a chain sits at a table full of vials, expert reports and pressed plants.

“Dr. Varga. The precinct pays me to know what's in these vials. And to keep investigators from drinking the wrong thing.”
Eine Frau, die eben noch Blumen verkauft: A woman who was just selling flowers suddenly stands beside you. Porcelain flashes beneath her veil.

Eine Gestalt mit weißer Halbmaske verbeu: A figure with a white half mask bows exaggeratedly low. “Applause, applause! Sadly the investigator must leave the performance early.”
Eine Gestalt unter einem schwarzen Schle: A figure under a black veil, still as a lamppost. "You're the policeman who asks questions better left unasked. Some people here would gladly sell you answers."
Eine Karteikarte aus dem Revier mit zehn: An index card from the precinct with ten black prints. How did it end up on the street?
Eine Krähe aus Glas landet auf einem Ast: A crow of glass lands on a branch and tilts its head. Starlight refracts in its body. It has been watching you for a long time.
Eine Krähe aus gefalteten Zeitungen hüpf: A crow of folded newspapers hops up to your feet. On its wing you read the word “tomorrow”.
Eine Krähenfeder aus klarem Glas. Sie kl: A crow feather of clear glass. It tinkles when the wind blows.

Eine Rabenfeder aus einer Pestmaske, get: A raven feather from a plague mask, soaked in vinegar and cloves.

Eine Spieldose aus Nussholz. Sie spielt: A music box of walnut. It plays a lullaby you've heard somewhere before.
Eine Spinne aus lila Garn und Messingnad: A spider of lilac yarn and brass needles crawls down a house wall. Its eye is a single glowing pearl.
Eine Spule glimmendes Garn. Mrs. Gorse w: A spool of glowing yarn. Mrs. Gorse would give a lot for it, she says.
Eine Stola aus Fuchsfell, die Glasaugen: A fox fur stole, its glass eyes still watching you.
Eine Tafel mit Preisen in Salz statt Sch: A board with prices in salt instead of shillings. At the very bottom: "Whoever hears a bell ring in the mudflats doesn't come back. Whoever hears it ring twice should ask Ole."
Eine Tapferkeitsmedaille der Stadtpolize: A medal for bravery from the city police. The bearer's name has been filed off.

At the very bottom, in shaky writing: “A silver tuning fork. Hums at night. Please don't sell.” Beside it someone has drawn an eye in a circle in pencil and erased it again.

Eine hagere Frau mit Lupe im Auge sieht: A gaunt woman with a loupe in her eye doesn't look up. “If you want to pawn something, put it on the counter. If you want to buy something, show me your money. If you're from the police, show me both.”
Eine halbe Maske, dünn wie Eierschale. Y: A half mask, thin as eggshell. Ysolde gave it to you. It is warm.
Eine halbe Porzellanmaske hinter einem g: Half a porcelain mask behind a grey veil

Eine zusammengesunkene Gestalt aus graue: A slumped figure of grey candle wax shuffles closer. A wick burns on its head, and its face drips.
